options.metric: Annual absolute reported deaths: sum number_of_motorist_killed or number_of_cyclist_killed across crash records, by category and calendar year, 2013–2025.
options.grouping: Calendar year of crash_date and category defined by the motorist or cyclist killed-count field.
options.reason: Absolute annual counts directly answer which group had more reported deaths in each year and show how that gap changed.
options.answer: Reported motorist deaths exceeded cyclist deaths in all 13 years; in 2025 the counts were 81 motorist deaths and 23 cyclist deaths, with respective series highs of 139 in 2020 and 31 in both 2019 and 2023.
options.interpretation: This directly compares absolute reported deaths by calendar year: the plotted motorist and cyclist values are the sums of their respective killed-count fields across all police-reported crashes with crash_date from 2013 through 2025 inclusive, with no denominator. Motorist deaths exceed cyclist deaths in all 13 years; motorist deaths peak at 139 in 2020, while cyclist deaths peak at 31 in both 2019 and 2023. Absolute counts are a defensible measure of annual burden, but they do not compare per-trip or per-person risk because travel exposure is not provided. The check found 2,132,218 in-scope crash rows, zero missing values in either death field, zero missing crash dates and zero dates at 1970-01-01 within scope, and date bounds spanning January 1–December 31 in every year; all in-scope rows were retained, although date bounds alone do not establish reporting completeness.

options.metric: Annual percentage of combined reported motorist and cyclist deaths attributable to each category, 2013–2025.
options.denominator: For each calendar year, the sum of reported motorist deaths and reported cyclist deaths; excludes all other road-user categories.
options.grouping: Calendar year of crash_date and category defined by the motorist or cyclist killed-count field.
options.reason: Annual shares make the composition of motorist-versus-cyclist deaths comparable even when the combined yearly totals differ.
options.answer: Cyclists accounted for 9.1% of combined motorist-and-cyclist deaths in 2013, reached a high of 27.4% in 2019, and accounted for 22.1% in 2025.
options.interpretation: This partly answers the year-by-year comparison as composition: for each calendar year of police-reported crashes dated 2013–2025 inclusive, each category's reported deaths are divided by that year's combined motorist and cyclist deaths. Cyclists' share was 9.1% in 2013, peaked at 27.4% in 2019, and was 22.1% in 2025, with motorist deaths making up the remainder. This share is a defensible way to compare the two categories' composition across years, but it does not show absolute death counts, deaths among other road users, or per-trip/per-person risk. The check found 2,132,218 in-scope crash rows, zero missing values in either death field, zero missing crash dates and zero dates at 1970-01-01 within scope, and date bounds spanning January 1–December 31 in every year; all in-scope rows were retained, though full date bounds do not establish reporting completeness.
